hazards.summary: Iceland weather changes rapidly; strong winds, rain, and sudden temperature drops are common, especially in winter.
mitigations: Check weather forecasts (vedur.is) before heading out, especially for remote areas.
Carry layered clothing: waterproof/windproof shell, warm mid-layer, thermal base layer.
Be prepared for sudden weather changes even in summer.
Avoid driving in severe weather conditions.

hazards.summary: Geothermal areas (hot springs, geysers, volcanoes) present burn risks from hot ground and steam.
mitigations: Stay on marked tracks and boardwalks in geothermal areas.
Keep safe distance from geysers, hot springs, and steam vents.
Supervise children and pets closely in thermal areas.
Be aware of unstable ground near thermal features.

hazards.summary: Remote areas have limited fuel and supply access; long distances between services, especially in the Highlands.
mitigations: Plan fuel stops before entering remote areas (F-roads, Highlands).
Carry extra food, water, and emergency supplies.
Check road conditions (road.is) before heading to remote areas.
Have offline maps and GPS backup.

hazards.summary: Strong ocean currents and unpredictable waves at black sand beaches; river crossings in Highlands can be dangerous.
mitigations: Never turn your back to the ocean at black sand beaches.
Stay away from the water's edge, especially at Reynisfjara.
Do not attempt river crossings in Highlands without proper vehicle and experience.
Check tide times and weather conditions before visiting coastal areas.

hazards.summary: F-roads (Highland roads) require 4x4 vehicles and are closed in winter; gravel roads and strong winds can be challenging.
mitigations: Rent appropriate vehicle (4x4 for F-roads, sturdy car for gravel roads).
Check road conditions and F-road status before departure.
Drive slowly on gravel roads and be cautious of strong crosswinds.
Never drive off-road or on closed roads.
